title: Angel Kaomoji ଘ(੭ˊᵕˋ)੭: Copy & Paste Winged Text Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste angel kaomoji: text faces with wings like ଘ(੭ˊᵕˋ)੭ and ꒰ঌ(˶ˆᗜˆ˵)໒꒱, winged bunnies and angels with magic wands. Click any face to copy it.
hero_tagline: Text faces with wings: ଘ(੭ˊᵕˋ)੭, ꒰ঌ ໒꒱ and ʚ ɞ wing frames, and angels holding a wand. Click any face to copy it.
intro: An angel kaomoji is a text face with wings drawn from letters of other alphabets. The Odia letters ଘ and ଓ curl outward like a wing on each side, ੭ is a Gurmukhi digit that reads as a raised arm, and pairs like ꒰ঌ ໒꒱ or ʚ ɞ frame the whole face like a pair of wings. Every face below is plain Unicode text, so it pastes into a bio, caption, comment or chat like any other character. Unicode has no halo character of its own, so for a halo use the 😇 emoji on the halo emoji page linked at the bottom.

sections.label: Winged Angels
sections.intro: The classic angel shape: a wing on the left and a raised arm or second wing on the right.

sections.label: Wing Frames
sections.intro: Here the wings wrap the whole face. ꒰ঌ and ໒꒱ come from Yi, Bengali and Lao, and ʚ ɞ are two rounded Latin letters that face each other.

sections.label: Magic Wands
sections.intro: A wing on one side and a wand on the other, for a wish, a blessing or a little bit of magic in a message.

sections.label: Accents
sections.intro: No face, just the wings. Put one before or after a name, or at the end of a caption.

faq.a: It is an angel: ଘ is the wing, ˊᵕˋ is a smiling face and the two ੭ are arms raised in a wave. People send it to mean something sweet or innocent, or as a thank-you.

faq.q: Is there a halo character I can put above a kaomoji?
faq.a: No. Unicode has no halo character, and plain text cannot stack one character above another reliably. Use the 😇 emoji beside the face instead.

faq.q: Why do some angel kaomoji show boxes on my friend's phone?
faq.a: Each face needs a font for every script it borrows from: ଘ and ଓ are Odia, ੭ is Gurmukhi, ꒰ ꒱ are Yi and ໒ is a Lao digit. A device without one of those fonts draws a box in that spot. The Smiling Angel ˙˚ʚ(´◡`)ɞ˚˙ and the Winged Heart ˚ʚ♡ɞ˚ use only Latin letters and common symbols, so they are the safest choice when you cannot check the reader's device.
